steps.label: Identify the appendix
steps.detail: State whether the appendix is completely, partially or not visualised, and where it lies.
steps.look: Ultrasound: follow the caecum to the appendiceal base with graded compression and trace to the tip, including retrocaecal and pelvic positions. CT: follow the caecal pole to the tip on multiplanar images.
steps.normal: Normal appendix visualised from base to tip.
findings: Appendix visualised in a [retrocaecal / pelvic / subhepatic] position; tip included.
Appendix only partially visualised; the tip is not seen.
Appendix not visualised; this does not exclude appendicitis.
steps.tip: A non-visualised appendix is not a normal appendix; say which part was not seen.

steps.label: Wall, lumen and appendicolith
steps.detail: Assess outer diameter, compressibility, wall layers, flow or enhancement and appendicolith.
steps.look: True short-axis image of the appendix with and without compression; Doppler of the wall; CT axial and coronal images.
steps.normal: Appendix compressible with an outer diameter below 6 mm and a preserved layered wall.
findings: Non-compressible appendix with outer diameter __ mm and mural hyperaemia, compatible with acute appendicitis.
Appendicolith __ mm at the [base / mid / tip].
Loss of the layered wall structure, raising concern for gangrenous appendicitis.
steps.tip: Inflammation can be confined to the tip; examine the whole length.

steps.label: Periappendiceal fat and fluid
steps.detail: Look for inflamed (echogenic, non-compressible) fat, local fluid and caecal wall reaction.
steps.look: Ultrasound around the appendix and caecal pole with compression; CT fat stranding around the appendix.
steps.normal: No periappendiceal fat inflammation or fluid.
findings: Echogenic, non-compressible inflamed fat surrounding the appendix.
Small volume of periappendiceal fluid.
Reactive thickening of the caecal pole.
steps.tip: Inflamed fat is one of the most reliable ultrasound signs; the appendix is often found at its centre.

steps.label: Complications
steps.detail: Assess wall defect, extraluminal gas or appendicolith, phlegmon, abscess and obstruction.
steps.look: Ultrasound and CT around the appendix and in the pelvis for collections; bowel calibre for obstruction.
steps.normal: No perforation, abscess, phlegmon or obstruction.
findings: Periappendiceal abscess __ × __ × __ mm in the [right iliac fossa / pelvis].
Focal wall defect with extraluminal gas or appendicolith, compatible with perforation.
Inflammatory phlegmon without a drainable collection.
Small-bowel dilatation from the inflamed appendix (adynamic or mechanical).

steps.label: Mimics and alternative diagnoses
steps.detail: Review the terminal ileum, caecum and colon, epiploic fat, ureter and adnexa when the appendix is normal or not seen.
steps.look: Terminal ileum and caecal wall; colonic diverticula; focal fat lesions; right ureter and kidney; adnexa in women.
steps.normal: No alternative cause for the symptoms identified.
findings: Terminal ileal and caecal wall thickening with enlarged nodes, compatible with bacterial ileocaecitis.
Enlarged mesenteric nodes without another abnormality (mesenteric lymphadenitis).
Epiploic appendagitis: oval non-compressible fat lesion with a hyperechoic or hyperattenuating rim at the site of tenderness.
Right-sided colonic diverticulitis.
steps.tip: Right-sided diverticulitis, epiploic appendagitis and omental infarction mimic appendicitis clinically but are usually treated conservatively.

steps.label: Solid organs
steps.detail: Map lacerations, haematomas, devascularisation and hilar injury in the liver, spleen, kidneys and pancreas.
steps.look: Portal venous phase organ by organ; arterial phase for vascular injury; excretory phase for the kidneys when acquired.
steps.normal: Liver, spleen, kidneys, adrenals and pancreas intact.
findings: Splenic laceration __ cm deep with subcapsular haematoma covering about __% of the surface.
Liver laceration of segment [ ], __ cm deep, [not] involving the hepatic veins.
Renal laceration extending into the collecting system [with urinary extravasation on the excretory phase].
Pancreatic laceration at the [neck / body] raising concern for duct injury.
steps.tip: Describe the injury features first; the grade follows from them.

steps.label: Vascular injury
steps.detail: Distinguish active extravasation from a contained pseudoaneurysm or arteriovenous fistula using the change between phases.
steps.look: Compare arterial and portal venous phases: active bleeding grows and changes shape; a pseudoaneurysm keeps its shape and follows the blood pool.
steps.normal: No active extravasation, pseudoaneurysm or major vascular injury.
findings: Active arterial extravasation from the [ ] enlarging on the portal venous phase.
Contained vascular injury (pseudoaneurysm) in the [ ], __ mm.
Injury of the [renal artery / hilum] with [devascularisation / thrombosis].
steps.tip: Active extravasation changes shape and increases in size between phases; a pseudoaneurysm does not.

steps.label: Haemoperitoneum and haematoma
steps.detail: Describe haemoperitoneum distribution, retroperitoneal haematoma and the sentinel clot.
steps.look: Perihepatic, perisplenic, paracolic and pelvic spaces; the densest clot is usually next to the bleeding organ.
steps.normal: No haemoperitoneum or retroperitoneal haematoma.
findings: Haemoperitoneum in the [ ], with a sentinel clot adjacent to the [spleen / liver / mesentery].
Retroperitoneal haematoma in zone [1 / 2 / 3].
Small volume of free fluid without a solid-organ injury; bowel or mesenteric injury should be considered.
steps.tip: Free fluid without a solid-organ injury in a male trauma patient should raise suspicion of bowel or mesenteric injury.

steps.label: Bowel, mesentery and urinary tract
steps.detail: Look for bowel wall discontinuity, abnormal enhancement, free gas, mesenteric haematoma and urinary tract leak.
steps.look: Bowel loops and mesentery in lung and soft-tissue windows; excretory phase for the collecting system; CT cystography for bladder injury.
steps.normal: No bowel or mesenteric injury; no free gas; no urinary extravasation.
findings: Focal bowel wall defect with extraluminal gas at the [ ], compatible with perforation.
Mesenteric haematoma with bowel wall thickening and reduced enhancement.
Extraperitoneal bladder rupture with contrast extravasation into the perivesical space (CT cystography).
Bladder injury cannot be excluded: routine excretory filling is not a CT cystogram.
steps.tip: Routine excretory contrast in the bladder is not equivalent to a properly performed CT cystogram.

steps.label: Associated injuries and grade
steps.detail: Review the diaphragm, great vessels, bones and penetrating trajectory, then assign the organ-specific grade with its year.
steps.look: Coronal and sagittal reformats for the diaphragm (collar and dependent-viscera signs); bone windows; trajectory for penetrating injury.
steps.normal: Diaphragm intact; no aortic, pelvic or spinal injury in the field of view.
findings: Left hemidiaphragm rupture with herniation of the [stomach / colon] (collar sign).
AAST [organ] injury grade [ ] (2018 revision) based on [features].
Associated fractures: [ ].
steps.tip: State the AAST revision used; grades from different years are not interchangeable.

steps.label: Pain localisation
steps.detail: Correlate the symptomatic quadrant with the imaging and confirm or exclude its most common cause first.
steps.look: Start where it hurts: right lower quadrant for appendicitis, left lower quadrant for diverticulitis, right upper quadrant for cholecystitis.
steps.normal: No abnormality at the site of pain.
findings: Findings at the site of maximal pain in the [ ] quadrant: [ ].
Pain site [ ]; no matching abnormality — see alternative findings below.
steps.tip: Confirm or exclude the most common disease for the pain location before surveying for general signs.

steps.label: Bowel and appendix
steps.detail: Review appendicitis, diverticulitis, obstruction and focal bowel inflammation.
steps.look: Appendix, colon with diverticula, small bowel calibre and wall; look for inflamed fat as a pointer.
steps.normal: Normal appendix; no bowel wall thickening, diverticulitis or obstruction.
findings: Acute appendicitis: non-compressible appendix __ mm with surrounding inflamed fat.
Sigmoid diverticulitis with an inflamed diverticulum and pericolic fat stranding [with / without] a pericolic abscess.
Small-bowel obstruction with a transition point at [ ].
Infectious ileocaecitis: thickened terminal ileum and caecum with enlarged nodes.
steps.tip: Inflamed fat is the best pointer to the site of disease on both ultrasound and CT.

steps.label: Solid organs
steps.detail: Inspect the liver, gallbladder, bile ducts, pancreas and spleen within the examination.
steps.look: Right upper quadrant organs and pancreas; correlate with focal tenderness.
steps.normal: Liver, gallbladder, bile ducts, pancreas and spleen unremarkable.
findings: Acute cholecystitis: distended gallbladder with wall thickening, an impacted stone and a positive sonographic Murphy sign.
Acute pancreatitis with peripancreatic fat stranding.
Dilated common bile duct __ mm.

steps.label: Urinary tract and pelvis
steps.detail: Check for obstructed urinary drainage and relevant pelvic causes.
steps.look: Kidneys and ureters for hydronephrosis and stone; adnexa and pelvic structures.
steps.normal: No hydronephrosis or urinary stone; pelvic structures unremarkable.
findings: Right [ ] hydronephrosis with a __ mm stone at the [ureterovesical junction].
Adnexal abnormality: [ ].
Pelvic inflammatory change with a tubo-ovarian collection.

steps.label: Peritoneum and vessels
steps.detail: Look for free gas, fluid, collections and vascular causes such as a leaking aneurysm or mesenteric ischaemia.
steps.look: Lung windows for free gas; dependent spaces for fluid; aorta and mesenteric vessels.
steps.normal: No free gas, ascites or collection; aorta and mesenteric vessels unremarkable.
findings: Free intraperitoneal gas, compatible with perforation of a hollow viscus [likely source: ].
Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm with retroperitoneal haematoma.
Occlusion of the superior mesenteric artery with poorly enhancing small bowel.
steps.tip: Free gas in the upper abdomen anterior to the liver is best seen with lung windows.

steps.label: Primary tumour
steps.detail: Document the epicentre (anal canal or margin), greatest dimension, length and circumferential extent.
steps.look: Small-field T2 oblique axial images perpendicular to the anal canal and coronal images parallel to it; DWI to confirm extent.
findings: Anal canal tumour, epicentre at the [level], greatest dimension __ cm, craniocaudal length __ cm, from __ to __ o'clock.
Anal margin tumour extending to the perianal skin.
Tumour extends cranially into the lower rectum __ cm above the anorectal junction.
steps.tip: T category depends on tumour size: measure the greatest dimension in any plane.

steps.label: Sphincter complex
steps.detail: Map involvement of the internal sphincter, intersphincteric plane, external sphincter and puborectalis.
steps.look: Coronal and axial T2 images through the sphincter layers.
findings: Tumour confined to the internal sphincter.
Tumour crosses the intersphincteric plane into the external sphincter at __ o'clock.
Involvement of the puborectalis/levator ani.
steps.tip: Sphincter involvement is important for treatment planning but is not T4 disease.

steps.label: Adjacent organs
steps.detail: Check for direct invasion of the vagina, urethra, prostate, bladder or skin.
steps.look: Axial and sagittal T2 images of the anterior boundary; look for loss of the fat plane with tumour signal within the organ wall.
steps.normal: No invasion of adjacent organs.
findings: Direct invasion of the posterior vaginal wall (T4).
Tumour abuts the [prostate / urethra] without definite invasion.
Extension to the perianal skin and ischioanal fat.

steps.label: Regional nodes
steps.detail: Review mesorectal, internal iliac/obturator, external iliac and inguinal stations; describe non-regional nodes separately.
steps.look: Axial T2 and DWI from the aortic bifurcation to the inguinal regions; the field must include the groins.
steps.normal: No suspicious mesorectal, pelvic sidewall or inguinal nodes.
findings: Suspicious [left inguinal] node, short axis __ mm, with [irregular border / heterogeneous signal / round shape].
Suspicious mesorectal and internal iliac nodes.
Enlarged common iliac or para-aortic node (non-regional, M1 if confirmed).
steps.tip: Inguinal nodes are regional in anal cancer, unlike in rectal cancer.

steps.label: Staging summary
steps.detail: Summarise imaging T and N with the named TNM edition and state what distant staging is available.
steps.look: Combine size, organ invasion and nodal stations; distant disease needs CT or PET-CT.
findings: Imaging stage cT__ N__ (TNM [edition]); distant staging on [CT / PET-CT] [pending / negative].
Extent uncertain at the [ ]; [ ] would clarify it.

steps.label: Defect type
steps.detail: Distinguish primary (umbilical, epigastric, Spigelian, lumbar) from incisional defects and from rectus diastasis.
steps.look: Axial and sagittal CT through the midline and prior incisions; note mesh and scars.
steps.normal: No abdominal wall hernia or rectus diastasis.
findings: Primary [umbilical / epigastric / Spigelian / lumbar] hernia.
Incisional hernia at the [midline laparotomy / stoma site / port site].
Rectus diastasis with an inter-rectus distance of __ mm, without a fascial defect.
steps.tip: Rectus diastasis is widening of the linea alba without a fascial defect; it is not a hernia.

steps.label: Defect location and size
steps.detail: Identify every defect and its position; measure the fascial aperture in transverse and craniocaudal dimensions.
steps.look: Axial images for transverse width and sagittal images for length, measured at the fascial edges; relate to the umbilicus and costal margin or pubis.
findings: Midline defect __ mm wide (transverse) and __ mm long (craniocaudal), [supra-/peri-/infraumbilical].
Multiple defects: [locations and sizes].
Rectus-to-defect ratio [ ] (combined rectus width divided by defect width).
steps.tip: Measure the fascial neck, not the sac: a wide sac often has a narrow neck.

steps.label: Sac contents
steps.detail: Identify herniated structures and any obstructive effect.
steps.look: Follow bowel loops into and out of the sac; estimate the proportion of viscera outside the abdominal cavity.
findings: Sac contains [fat / small bowel / transverse colon / omentum].
Loss of domain: about __% of the visceral volume lies within the hernia sac.
Transition to collapsed bowel at the hernia neck.
steps.tip: Loss of domain affects whether the contents can be reduced and how the repair is planned.

steps.label: Abdominal wall muscles and mesh
steps.detail: Assess the rectus and lateral muscles, previous mesh and scarring relevant to repair.
steps.look: Axial images of the rectus muscles and the external oblique, internal oblique and transversus layers.
steps.normal: Rectus and lateral abdominal wall muscles of normal bulk; no mesh.
findings: Rectus width [right __ mm / left __ mm]; lateral muscle atrophy [ ].
Previous [onlay / sublay / intraperitoneal] mesh with recurrence at its [edge].
Mesh infection: fluid and gas along the mesh.

steps.label: Complications
steps.detail: Assess bowel enhancement, sac fluid, fat stranding and signs of incarceration or strangulation.
steps.look: Bowel within the sac: wall thickening and enhancement compared with other loops; fluid and stranding in the sac.
steps.normal: No incarceration, obstruction or strangulation.
findings: Incarcerated small bowel with upstream obstruction.
Reduced wall enhancement, sac fluid and mesenteric stranding, raising concern for strangulation.
Enteroatmospheric fistula at [ ].
steps.tip: Fluid in the sac with mesenteric stranding and poorly enhancing bowel suggests strangulation.

steps.label: Clinical context
steps.detail: Record whether the lesion is incidental, found during cancer staging or in an endocrine work-up, and any prior imaging.
steps.look: Referral information and all prior imaging that includes the adrenals.
findings: Incidental adrenal lesion; no known malignancy.
Adrenal lesion in a patient with known [malignancy], found on staging.
Endocrine work-up for [hypertension / Cushing / hyperaldosteronism / phaeochromocytoma].
steps.tip: A benign-appearing lesion can still be hormonally active; imaging does not replace biochemical testing.

steps.label: Morphology
steps.detail: Describe side, size, homogeneity, margins, necrosis, haemorrhage, calcification and macroscopic fat.
steps.look: Axial and coronal images of both adrenals.
steps.normal: Normal adrenal glands without a focal lesion.
findings: [Right / left] adrenal nodule __ mm, homogeneous and well defined.
Myelolipoma: adrenal lesion with macroscopic fat.
Heterogeneous adrenal mass __ mm with necrosis and calcification.
Adrenal cyst with a thin wall and fluid attenuation.
steps.tip: Macroscopic fat in an adrenal mass is diagnostic of myelolipoma.

steps.label: Lipid characterisation
steps.detail: Measure unenhanced attenuation, or assess signal loss on chemical-shift MRI.
steps.look: Unenhanced CT with a large ROI over at least half of the lesion avoiding edges; in- and opposed-phase MRI.
findings: Unenhanced attenuation __ HU (10 HU or less), diagnostic of a lipid-rich adenoma.
Signal loss on opposed-phase MRI, compatible with an adenoma.
Unenhanced attenuation __ HU; lipid-poor lesion, indeterminate.
steps.tip: An unenhanced attenuation of 10 HU or less indicates a lipid-rich adenoma; no further imaging is needed for that lesion.

steps.label: Contrast behaviour and discordant features
steps.detail: Interpret washout only with its protocol and context, and list features that do not fit an adenoma.
steps.look: Portal venous and 15-minute delayed phases if acquired; absolute washout 60% or more and relative washout 40% or more favour adenoma.
findings: Absolute washout __% and relative washout __% on a dedicated adrenal protocol.
Washout values favour adenoma but the lesion is heterogeneous; discordant features remain.
Marked enhancement with high T2 signal; phaeochromocytoma should be excluded biochemically.
steps.tip: Washout overlaps between adenomas and other lesions; do not rely on it when morphology is atypical.

steps.label: Growth and local extent
steps.detail: Compare size with prior studies and assess local invasion, nodes and the other adrenal.
steps.look: Same plane and window as the prior study; renal vein and IVC; the contralateral adrenal.
steps.normal: Stable size compared with [date]; no local invasion; contralateral adrenal normal.
findings: Growth from __ mm to __ mm since [date] (__ mm, __%).
Invasion of the [IVC / renal vein / kidney], raising concern for adrenocortical carcinoma.
Bilateral adrenal nodules.
steps.tip: A lesion larger than 4 cm, heterogeneous or growing raises concern for malignancy.

steps.label: Aneurysm
steps.detail: Define the involved aortic segment, morphology and maximal outer diameter.
steps.look: Double-oblique multiplanar reformats perpendicular to the centreline; measure outer wall to outer wall.
findings: Infrarenal fusiform abdominal aortic aneurysm, maximum outer diameter __ mm.
Juxtarenal / suprarenal extension with a __ mm neck.
Saccular aneurysm of the [ ] segment.
steps.tip: Axial diameters overestimate a tortuous aorta; measure perpendicular to the centreline.

steps.label: Rupture
steps.detail: Identify active extravasation and retroperitoneal or intraperitoneal haemorrhage.
steps.look: Retroperitoneum around the aneurysm and psoas, perirenal and pararenal spaces; arterial phase for contrast leak.
steps.normal: No periaortic haematoma or extravasation.
findings: Ruptured aneurysm with a left retroperitoneal haematoma extending into the [perirenal / pararenal] space.
Active contrast extravasation from the [left posterolateral] aneurysm wall.
Periaortic stranding without haematoma; contained leak cannot be excluded.
steps.tip: The absence of active extravasation does not exclude a contained rupture.

steps.label: Wall and thrombus (impending rupture)
steps.detail: Review wall continuity and signs of impending rupture: high-attenuating crescent, focal calcification discontinuity, tangential calcium sign and draped aorta.
steps.look: Unenhanced images if available for the crescent; contrast images for wall contour and calcification.
steps.normal: Intact aneurysm wall; no signs of impending rupture.
findings: High-attenuating crescent within the mural thrombus, a sign of impending rupture.
Focal discontinuity of circumferential wall calcification.
Draped aorta: the posterior wall drapes over the vertebral body without an intervening fat plane.
steps.tip: A hyperattenuating crescent in the thrombus or wall indicates acute bleeding into it and imminent rupture.

steps.label: Branch vessels
steps.detail: Describe renal and visceral artery relationships and organ perfusion.
steps.look: Coronal and sagittal reformats at the coeliac, SMA and renal origins.
steps.normal: Coeliac, SMA and renal arteries arise from a non-aneurysmal aorta and are patent; organs enhance normally.
findings: Aneurysm neck __ mm below the lowest renal artery; neck length __ mm.
Accessory renal artery arising from the aneurysm.
Renal or bowel hypoperfusion.

steps.label: Iliac arteries and adjacent structures
steps.detail: Assess iliac extension, access-vessel calibre and possible fistulation to bowel or vein.
steps.look: Common, internal and external iliac and common femoral arteries; duodenum and IVC next to the aneurysm.
steps.normal: Iliac arteries non-aneurysmal and suitable in calibre; no fistula.
findings: Common iliac artery aneurysm, [right / left], __ mm.
External iliac artery diameter __ mm (access).
Loss of the fat plane with the duodenum and gas in the aneurysm sac, raising concern for aortoenteric fistula.

steps.label: Duct visibility
steps.detail: State which segments of the common bile duct are directly seen.
steps.look: Subcostal and intercostal windows, patient in left posterior oblique or upright position to move duodenal gas; follow the duct to the pancreatic head.
steps.normal: Common bile duct visualised along its whole course to the papilla.
findings: Proximal and mid common bile duct visualised; the distal duct is obscured by bowel gas.
Distal duct seen to the pancreatic head.
steps.tip: A distal duct that is not seen cannot be reported as stone-free.

steps.label: Duct calibre
steps.detail: Measure the common bile duct and assess intrahepatic dilatation.
steps.look: Measure inner wall to inner wall, perpendicular to the duct, at its widest visible point; look for parallel-channel sign in the liver.
steps.normal: Common bile duct __ mm (normal); no intrahepatic duct dilatation.
findings: Dilated common bile duct __ mm with intrahepatic duct dilatation.
Common bile duct __ mm after cholecystectomy, without intrahepatic dilatation.
steps.tip: Duct calibre increases with age and after cholecystectomy; interpret it with the clinical and laboratory context.

steps.label: Intraductal contents
steps.detail: Look for an echogenic stone with shadowing, sludge or mobile contents.
steps.look: Scan along the duct in longitudinal and transverse planes; change patient position to show mobility.
steps.normal: No intraductal stone or sludge.
findings: Echogenic __ mm stone with acoustic shadowing in the distal common bile duct.
Intraductal sludge without shadowing.

steps.label: Gallbladder
steps.detail: Look for source stones and signs of recent passage or ongoing obstruction.
steps.look: Gallbladder in two positions; wall and pericholecystic region.
steps.normal: Gallbladder without stones; normal wall.
findings: Multiple gallstones; gallbladder not distended.
Contracted gallbladder with wall thickening after recent colic.
steps.tip: After a passed stone, the duct may still be dilated while the gallbladder looks normal.

steps.label: Obstruction and complications
steps.detail: Assess the level of obstruction and associated pancreatitis, cholangitis or Mirizzi syndrome.
steps.look: Pancreatic head and body; hepatic duct at the gallbladder neck; liver for abscess.
steps.normal: No biliary obstruction, pancreatitis or cholangitis features.
findings: Obstruction at the level of the distal common bile duct by a stone.
Enlarged hypoechoic pancreas, compatible with biliary pancreatitis.
Stone impacted in the cystic duct compressing the common hepatic duct (Mirizzi syndrome).

steps.label: Contents and gallbladder neck
steps.detail: Assess the mobility of stones or sludge and look for a stone impacted in the neck.
steps.look: Supine and left lateral decubitus scanning; follow the gallbladder into the neck and cystic duct.
steps.normal: No gallstones or sludge.
findings: Multiple mobile gallstones, largest __ mm.
Stone impacted in the gallbladder neck, not moving with position change.
Sludge layering in the dependent gallbladder.
steps.tip: An impacted neck stone does not move when the patient turns; this is the key to obstruction.

steps.label: Distension
steps.detail: Assess gallbladder size and shape (hydrops).
steps.look: Transverse diameter and shape: a rounded gallbladder is distended.
steps.normal: Gallbladder not distended.
findings: Distended, rounded gallbladder (transverse diameter __ mm), compatible with hydrops.

steps.label: Wall
steps.detail: Describe focal or diffuse wall thickening, layers and vascularity.
steps.look: Measure the anterior wall perpendicular to its surface; Doppler for hyperaemia.
steps.normal: Gallbladder wall not thickened.
findings: Diffuse wall thickening __ mm with a striated appearance.
Focal wall thickening with comet-tail artefacts, compatible with adenomyomatosis.
Irregular focal wall thickening or mass; gallbladder carcinoma should be considered.
steps.tip: Wall thickening alone is non-specific: a contracted gallbladder, hepatitis, heart failure and cirrhosis all cause it.

steps.label: Local inflammation
steps.detail: Check the sonographic Murphy sign, pericholecystic fluid and inflamed fat.
steps.look: Probe pressure directly over the gallbladder; pericholecystic fat and fluid.
steps.normal: Sonographic Murphy sign negative; no pericholecystic fluid.
findings: Positive sonographic Murphy sign with pericholecystic fluid: acute cholecystitis.
Intraluminal membranes and irregular wall: gangrenous cholecystitis.
Gas in the gallbladder wall: emphysematous cholecystitis.
Focal wall defect with pericholecystic collection: perforation.

steps.label: Bile ducts and systemic context
steps.detail: Review bile duct calibre and systemic causes of wall thickening.
steps.look: Common bile duct calibre; liver, ascites and signs of heart failure.
steps.normal: Common bile duct not dilated; no ascites.
findings: Common bile duct __ mm with intrahepatic dilatation.
Ascites and liver changes; wall thickening likely secondary to [cirrhosis / hepatitis / heart failure].

steps.label: Duct distribution
steps.detail: Map intrahepatic and extrahepatic abnormalities and whether dilatation is focal, segmental or diffuse.
steps.look: MRCP maximum-intensity projections and source images; CT or ultrasound duct-oriented images.
steps.normal: No intrahepatic or extrahepatic bile duct dilatation.
findings: Diffuse intrahepatic and extrahepatic duct dilatation to the level of [ ].
Segmental intrahepatic duct dilatation in [segments].

steps.label: Duct morphology
steps.detail: Characterise strictures, beading and cystic dilatation.
steps.look: Stricture site and length; alternating strictures and dilatations; saccular or fusiform cysts.
steps.normal: Normal duct calibre and contour.
findings: Multifocal short strictures with intervening dilatation (beaded appearance), compatible with primary sclerosing cholangitis.
Fusiform extrahepatic duct dilatation, compatible with a choledochal cyst (Todani type [ ]).
Saccular intrahepatic duct dilatation with the central dot sign, compatible with Caroli disease.
steps.tip: The central dot sign — portal radicles within dilated ducts — is characteristic of Caroli disease.

steps.label: Obstructing cause
steps.detail: Identify intraductal material, a mural lesion or external compression at the transition.
steps.look: Follow the duct to the transition; look for stone, enhancing wall thickening or an extrinsic mass.
steps.normal: No obstructing lesion.
findings: Hilar stricture with enhancing periductal soft tissue, compatible with hilar cholangiocarcinoma (Bismuth–Corlette type [ ]).
Intraductal stones in the [ ] duct.
Extrinsic compression by [ ].
steps.tip: Duct dilatation is a finding, not a diagnosis; the transition and its morphology point to the cause.

steps.label: Liver and vessels
steps.detail: Assess lobar atrophy, liver lesions and portal vein and hepatic artery involvement.
steps.look: Liver volume by lobe; portal and hepatic arterial relationships at the hilum.
steps.normal: No lobar atrophy, liver lesion or vascular involvement.
findings: Atrophy of the [left] lobe with crowded dilated ducts.
Encasement of the [right / left] portal vein by tumour.
Intrahepatic mass with capsular retraction and delayed enhancement.

steps.label: Context and complications
steps.detail: Record prior surgery, stents and signs of cholangitis, abscess or nodes.
steps.look: Surgical anatomy, stents and drains; periductal enhancement and liver abscesses.
steps.normal: No stent or prior biliary surgery; no cholangitis or abscess.
findings: Biliary stent in situ with pneumobilia.
Periductal enhancement and liver abscesses, compatible with cholangitis.
Enlarged hepatoduodenal ligament nodes.

steps.label: Lesion inventory
steps.detail: Number each lesion, record wall location, size, morphology and stalk.
steps.look: Small-field T2 in three planes with a well-distended bladder.
findings: Single [papillary / sessile] tumour on the [left lateral wall], __ mm, [with / without] a stalk.
Multiple tumours: [locations and sizes].

steps.label: T2 muscle interface
steps.detail: Assess the continuity of the low-T2 muscular layer beneath each lesion.
steps.look: High-resolution T2 perpendicular to the tumour base.
findings: Tumour with a stalk and thickened inner layer; the low-signal muscle is continuous (T2 score 1–2).
Loss of the low-signal muscle line beneath the tumour (T2 score 4).
Tumour extends through the muscle into the perivesical fat (T2 score 5).
steps.tip: A thickened, enhancing inner layer or stalk beneath the tumour indicates it is superficial.

steps.label: Diffusion
steps.detail: Look for concordant extension of restricted diffusion into the muscle.
steps.look: High-b-value DWI and ADC matched to the T2 plane.
findings: Restricted diffusion confined to the tumour with a low-signal stalk (DWI score 1–2).
Restricted diffusion extends focally into the muscular layer (DWI score 4).
Restricted diffusion extends to the perivesical fat (DWI score 5).
steps.tip: When T2 and DWI disagree, DWI is the dominant sequence for the final category.

steps.label: Dynamic contrast enhancement
steps.detail: Assess the early enhancement pattern at the tumour base.
steps.look: Early dynamic phase at the tumour–muscle interface.
findings: Early enhancement confined to the inner layer (DCE score 1–2).
Early enhancement extends focally into the muscular layer (DCE score 4).
Early enhancement extends through the wall into perivesical fat (DCE score 5).

steps.label: Extent and VI-RADS
steps.detail: Give the overall VI-RADS category and assess perivesical spread, adjacent organs, ureters and nodes.
steps.look: Integrate the three sequences; review the ureteric orifices, prostate or uterus, and pelvic nodes.
findings: Overall VI-RADS [2]: muscle invasion unlikely.
Overall VI-RADS [4]: muscle invasion likely.
Overall VI-RADS 5 with extravesical extension to the [ ].
Tumour at the [left] ureteric orifice with hydroureteronephrosis.
steps.tip: VI-RADS estimates the likelihood of muscle invasion; it is not a histological stage.

steps.label: Mesenteric arteries
steps.detail: Assess coeliac, SMA and IMA patency, emboli and ostial stenosis.
steps.look: Arterial phase axial and sagittal reformats along the SMA; emboli lodge a few centimetres beyond the origin.
steps.normal: Coeliac trunk, SMA and IMA patent.
findings: Abrupt occlusion of the SMA __ cm beyond its origin, compatible with embolism.
Thrombotic occlusion at the SMA origin on a background of atherosclerosis.
Patent vessels with diffuse narrowing (non-occlusive ischaemia in the appropriate setting).
steps.tip: An embolus typically lodges beyond the middle colic artery origin, sparing the proximal jejunum.

steps.label: Mesenteric and portal veins
steps.detail: Assess the SMV and portal vein for thrombosis and signs of venous congestion.
steps.look: Portal venous phase; mesenteric venous arcades and mesenteric oedema.
steps.normal: SMV and portal vein patent.
findings: Thrombus in the SMV extending into the portal vein, with mesenteric congestion.
Mesenteric venous engorgement without thrombus.

steps.label: Bowel wall enhancement
steps.detail: Map the affected segment and compare its enhancement with normal loops.
steps.look: Portal venous phase in soft-tissue window with narrow width; compare adjacent loops.
steps.normal: Normal enhancement of the bowel wall.
findings: Reduced/absent enhancement of a __ cm segment of [jejunum / ileum / colon].
Hyperenhancing, thickened bowel wall (reperfusion or venous congestion).
Paper-thin, non-enhancing wall, compatible with transmural infarction.
steps.tip: Absent wall enhancement is the most specific sign of ischaemia; compare with adjacent normal loops on the same phase.

steps.label: Wall, calibre and mesentery
steps.detail: Evaluate wall thickness, dilatation, mesenteric oedema and fluid.
steps.look: Wall thickness in distended segments; mesenteric fat and free fluid.
steps.normal: No bowel wall thickening, dilatation or mesenteric oedema.
findings: Thickened oedematous wall with a target appearance and mesenteric fluid.
Dilated fluid-filled loops with mesenteric oedema.

steps.label: Pneumatosis, venous gas and perforation
steps.detail: Look for pneumatosis, portomesenteric venous gas and perforation.
steps.look: Lung windows for gas in the wall, mesenteric and portal veins, and free gas.
steps.normal: No pneumatosis, portomesenteric venous gas or free gas.
findings: Pneumatosis of the [ ] with portal and mesenteric venous gas.
Free intraperitoneal gas, compatible with perforation.
steps.tip: Pneumatosis alone is not proof of infarction; interpret it with enhancement and the vascular findings.

steps.label: Length and distribution
steps.detail: Measure the length of involvement and name the affected bowel; length narrows the differential.
steps.look: Coronal reformats; follow the involved segment from start to end.
steps.normal: No bowel wall thickening.
findings: Focal thickening (under 5 cm) of the [ ] with [shouldering / tapering] margins.
Focal thickening over 5–10 cm of the [ ].
Segmental thickening over 10–30 cm of the [ ].
Diffuse thickening of the [entire colon / colon and small bowel].
steps.tip: Focal under 5 cm with shouldered margins suggests adenocarcinoma; 5–10 cm suggests diverticulitis, Crohn disease or ischaemia; diffuse colonic involvement suggests ulcerative colitis.

steps.label: Wall thickness and symmetry
steps.detail: Measure wall thickness and describe symmetry, regularity and margins.
steps.look: Measure perpendicular to a distended wall; compare with adjacent loops.
findings: Symmetric, regular wall thickening of __ mm, favouring a benign process.
Asymmetric, irregular or lobulated wall thickening of __ mm, raising concern for tumour.
steps.tip: Collapsed bowel looks thick; judge thickness only in a distended segment.

steps.label: Attenuation pattern
steps.detail: Describe the mural attenuation pattern: white (hyperenhancing), grey, water target, fat target or gas.
steps.look: Portal venous phase; note the phase actually acquired.
findings: White pattern: avid mucosal enhancement (e.g., active inflammatory bowel disease or shock bowel).
Grey pattern: homogeneous enhancement (e.g., tumour or chronic Crohn disease).
Water target: enhancing mucosa and serosa with submucosal oedema.
Fat target: submucosal fat deposition (chronic inflammatory bowel disease).
steps.tip: The attenuation pattern narrows the differential; combine it with length and degree of thickening.

steps.label: Mesentery and vessels
steps.detail: Assess surrounding fat, vessels and nodes.
steps.look: Mesenteric fat, vascular patency and engorgement (comb sign), and nodes.
steps.normal: Mesentery unremarkable; vessels patent; no significant nodes.
findings: Engorged vasa recta (comb sign) and fibrofatty proliferation.
Mesenteric fat stranding disproportionate to the wall thickening.
Mesenteric venous thrombosis.

steps.label: Lumen and complications
steps.detail: Review narrowing, upstream dilatation, collections and free gas.
steps.look: Lumen through the affected segment and upstream calibre; collections and free gas.
steps.normal: No narrowing, obstruction, collection or free gas.
findings: Luminal narrowing with upstream dilatation to __ mm.
Abscess __ mm adjacent to the affected segment.
Pneumatosis in the affected segment.

steps.label: Level and calibre
steps.detail: Identify small- or large-bowel obstruction and distal decompression.
steps.look: Coronal reformats; small bowel over 25 mm and colon over 60 mm (caecum over 90 mm) are dilated.
steps.normal: No dilated bowel.
findings: Dilated small bowel to __ mm with collapsed distal ileum and colon: small-bowel obstruction.
Dilated colon to __ mm at the [caecum] with collapsed distal colon: large-bowel obstruction.

steps.label: Transition point and cause
steps.detail: Find the transition point and name its cause.
steps.look: Follow dilated bowel to collapsed bowel on multiplanar images; the small-bowel faeces sign usually lies just proximal to the transition.
findings: Transition in the [right lower quadrant] without a visible cause, most likely adhesional.
Transition at an [inguinal / incisional] hernia neck.
Transition at an obstructing mass in the [ ].
steps.tip: The small-bowel faeces sign helps locate the transition point.

steps.label: Closed loop
steps.detail: Look for two adjacent transition points, a C- or U-shaped loop, radial mesenteric vessels and a whirl.
steps.look: Coronal and axial images of the loop configuration; mesenteric vessels converging towards one point.
steps.normal: No closed-loop configuration.
findings: Closed-loop obstruction: U-shaped dilated loop with two adjacent transition points and converging mesenteric vessels.
Whirl sign of the mesentery, compatible with volvulus.
Caecal / sigmoid volvulus.
steps.tip: A closed loop can involve a short segment without generalised dilatation.

steps.label: Viability
steps.detail: Assess wall enhancement, thickening, pneumatosis, mesenteric oedema and free fluid.
steps.look: Compare wall enhancement of the obstructed loop with normal bowel; mesentery for oedema.
steps.normal: Normal wall enhancement; no mesenteric oedema or free fluid.
findings: Reduced wall enhancement with mesenteric oedema and fluid, raising concern for strangulation.
Pneumatosis of the obstructed loop.
steps.tip: Preserved enhancement does not exclude evolving strangulation; mesenteric oedema and fluid are early signs.

steps.label: Complications and cause
steps.detail: Search for perforation and an obstructing hernia or tumour, and any additional transition.
steps.look: Hernia orifices, free gas and all bowel segments.
steps.normal: No free gas; no hernia or mass.
findings: Free gas, compatible with perforation.
Incarcerated small bowel in a [left inguinal] hernia.
Internal hernia: small bowel clustered in the [left paraduodenal] fossa.

steps.label: Bowel map
steps.detail: Map involved small-bowel segments, skip areas and anastomoses.
steps.look: Coronal T2 and post-contrast images with adequate distension; note segments that are poorly distended.
steps.normal: No small-bowel wall thickening or abnormal enhancement.
findings: Terminal ileal disease over __ cm.
Skip lesions in the [jejunum / ileum].
Neoterminal ileum at the ileocolic anastomosis involved over __ cm.
steps.tip: Poor distension can mimic wall thickening; confirm on more than one sequence.

steps.label: Mural activity
steps.detail: Integrate wall thickness, T2 mural oedema, ulcers, enhancement and diffusion.
steps.look: Fat-suppressed T2, DWI and post-contrast images of the involved segment.
findings: Active inflammation: wall thickening __ mm, mural oedema, ulcers and layered enhancement.
Wall thickening with homogeneous enhancement and low T2 signal, favouring chronic fibrotic disease.
steps.tip: Inflammation and fibrosis often coexist; diffusion alone does not quantify activity.

steps.label: Strictures
steps.detail: Identify fixed narrowing and upstream dilatation.
steps.look: Cine or repeated T2 images to show fixed narrowing; upstream calibre.
steps.normal: No stricture.
findings: Stricture of the [terminal ileum] __ cm long with upstream dilatation to __ mm.

steps.label: Penetrating disease
steps.detail: Trace sinus tracts and fistulae to their endpoints and look for abscesses.
steps.look: Fat-suppressed T2 and post-contrast images; follow each tract.
steps.normal: No sinus tract, fistula or abscess.
findings: Enteroenteric fistula between the [terminal ileum] and [sigmoid colon].
Abscess __ × __ × __ mm adjacent to the [ ].
Sinus tract ending blindly in the mesentery.

steps.label: Mesentery and interval change
steps.detail: Assess the comb sign, fibrofatty proliferation, nodes, extraintestinal findings and change since the prior study.
steps.look: Mesentery next to involved bowel; perianal region if covered; the prior study.
steps.normal: No mesenteric inflammation; no interval change.
findings: Comb sign and fibrofatty proliferation adjacent to the [terminal ileum].
Improvement in mural activity since [date].
Sacroiliitis / cholelithiasis / perianal fistula as extraintestinal findings.

steps.label: Coverage
steps.detail: Record which bowel segments were examined and which were limited.
steps.look: Systematic survey from the sigmoid to the caecum and terminal ileum, then the small bowel; graded compression.
steps.normal: Terminal ileum, colon and visible small bowel examined.
findings: Terminal ileum and colon examined; small bowel in the pelvis not assessable.

steps.label: Bowel wall
steps.detail: Assess wall thickness, layering and compressibility.
steps.look: Measure a single wall perpendicular to the lumen; look at the five-layer gut signature.
steps.normal: Normal bowel wall thickness and preserved layering.
findings: Terminal ileal wall thickening __ mm with preserved layering.
Wall thickening __ mm with loss of layering (transmural inflammation).
steps.tip: A normal ileal wall is thin (about 1.5 mm in the source example, against 6.5 mm in Crohn ileum); thickening alone is not specific to Crohn disease.

steps.label: Activity
steps.detail: Review mural hyperaemia, ulcers and inflamed mesenteric fat.
steps.look: Low-flow Doppler of the wall; echogenic fat surrounding the loop.
steps.normal: No mural hyperaemia or inflamed fat.
findings: Marked mural hyperaemia on Doppler.
Inflamed (echogenic, creeping) fat surrounding the [terminal ileum].
Deep ulcers with loss of the submucosal layer.

steps.label: Lumen and complications
steps.detail: Assess peristalsis, stenosis, upstream dilatation and penetrating disease.
steps.look: Real-time peristalsis; narrowing and upstream calibre; hypoechoic tracts and collections.
steps.normal: Normal peristalsis; no stenosis, fistula or collection.
findings: Stenosis with upstream dilatation to __ mm.
Hypoechoic tract extending from the ileum toward the [ ] (fistula).
Abscess __ mm in the [ ].

steps.label: Mimics and comparison
steps.detail: Check for appendicitis, infectious ileocolitis, diverticulitis and other mimics; compare with prior studies.
steps.look: Appendix, caecum, colon and mesenteric nodes.
steps.normal: No alternative cause; no change since [date].
findings: Infectious ileocaecitis: mucosal thickening with preserved layers and enlarged nodes.
Improvement in wall thickness and hyperaemia since [date].

steps.label: Primary site
steps.detail: Localise the lesion, identify multiplicity and measure it.
steps.look: Thin-section multiplanar CT; follow the small bowel from the duodenum to the ileum.
steps.normal: No small-bowel mass.
findings: Solitary mass in the [proximal jejunum], __ × __ mm, involving __ cm of bowel.
Multiple lesions in the [ ].

steps.label: Morphology and enhancement
steps.detail: Describe mural, polypoid or exophytic growth, enhancement and necrosis.
steps.look: Arterial and portal venous phases; mass attenuation and relation to the wall.
findings: Short annular narrowing with shouldered margins (adenocarcinoma pattern).
Exophytic hyperenhancing mass with central necrosis (GIST pattern).
Circumferential wall thickening with aneurysmal dilatation of the lumen (lymphoma pattern).
Small hyperenhancing ileal nodule (neuroendocrine tumour pattern).
steps.tip: Different tumours share appearances; describe the growth pattern rather than asserting a histology.

steps.label: Luminal effect
steps.detail: Assess obstruction, intussusception and aneurysmal dilatation.
steps.look: Lumen through the lesion and upstream calibre.
steps.normal: No obstruction or intussusception.
findings: Partial obstruction with upstream dilatation to __ mm.
Intussusception with the mass as lead point.

steps.label: Mesentery and nodes
steps.detail: Assess mesenteric mass, desmoplastic reaction, nodes and vessels.
steps.look: Mesentery next to the lesion; spiculated mass with calcification; vessel encasement.
steps.normal: No mesenteric mass or enlarged nodes.
findings: Spiculated calcified mesenteric mass with desmoplastic retraction (neuroendocrine tumour pattern).
Bulky mesenteric nodes encasing vessels without obstruction (lymphoma pattern).

steps.label: Spread
steps.detail: Inspect adjacent structures, the liver and peritoneum.
steps.look: Liver in arterial and portal phases; peritoneal surfaces.
steps.normal: No liver or peritoneal metastases.
findings: Hypervascular liver metastases.
Peritoneal deposits in the [ ].

steps.label: Object
steps.detail: Describe number, shape, dimensions and radio-opacity.
steps.look: CT with thin sections and multiplanar images in bone and soft-tissue windows; radiographs for opaque objects.
steps.normal: No foreign body identified.
findings: Linear hyperdense object __ mm long (for example a fish bone).
Radiolucent object seen only on CT as a linear [low-attenuation] structure.
steps.tip: Fish bones and toothpicks are thin; use thin sections and bone windows.

steps.label: Location
steps.detail: Identify the segment and the relation of the object to the bowel wall.
steps.look: Multiplanar images along the object: inside the lumen, crossing the wall or outside it.
findings: Object within the lumen of the [ ].
Object traversing the wall of the [terminal ileum / rectosigmoid].
steps.tip: Perforation usually occurs at angulations and narrowings: the ileocaecal region and rectosigmoid.

steps.label: Bowel effect
steps.detail: Assess wall thickening and obstruction.
steps.look: The bowel wall around the object and upstream calibre.
steps.normal: No bowel wall thickening or obstruction.
findings: Focal wall thickening around the object.
Obstruction at the level of the object.

steps.label: Perforation and collection
steps.detail: Look for local gas, inflammatory stranding and abscess.
steps.look: Lung windows for small gas bubbles; fat stranding and collections.
steps.normal: No perforation or collection.
findings: Localised perforation with a few extraluminal gas bubbles and fat stranding.
Abscess __ mm around the object.
steps.tip: Sharp objects can perforate with little free gas; localised stranding may be the only clue.

steps.label: Migration and adjacent organs
steps.detail: Trace proximity to vessels and organ penetration, and change since prior imaging.
steps.look: Relationship of the tip to the liver, vessels and adjacent organs; the prior study.
steps.normal: No adjacent organ or vessel involvement.
findings: Object penetrates into the [liver], with an abscess.
Tip lies adjacent to the [ ] vessel.

steps.label: Lung bases
steps.detail: Look above each hemidiaphragm for consolidation with air bronchograms.
steps.look: Intercostal scanning above the liver and spleen in longitudinal planes.
steps.normal: Normal aerated lung bases with A-lines; no consolidation.
findings: [Right / left] lower-lobe consolidation __ mm with dynamic air bronchograms, compatible with pneumonia.
Parapneumonic consolidation with an adjacent small effusion.
steps.tip: Dynamic air bronchograms (moving with respiration) favour pneumonia over atelectasis.

steps.label: Pleura
steps.detail: Assess pleural fluid, its echogenicity and lung sliding.
steps.look: Posterior costophrenic angles in the sitting or supine position; high-frequency probe for sliding.
steps.normal: No pleural effusion; lung sliding present.
findings: [Right / left] pleural effusion, depth __ mm, [anechoic / complex / septated].
Absent lung sliding at [ ]; pneumothorax should be considered.

steps.label: Peripheral lung lesions
steps.detail: Look for pleural-based hypoechoic lesions that may represent infarcts in suspected pulmonary embolism.
steps.look: Systematic intercostal scanning of the painful area and both lower lobes.
steps.normal: No pleural-based lung lesion.
findings: [Number] pleural-based, wedge-shaped hypoechoic lesions of __ mm in the [ ], suspicious for pulmonary infarcts; CT pulmonary angiography recommended.
steps.tip: A normal thoracic ultrasound does not exclude pulmonary embolism.

steps.label: Pericardium
steps.detail: Assess pericardial fluid from the subxiphoid window and signs of tamponade.
steps.look: Subxiphoid view of the heart; inferior vena cava for plethora.
steps.normal: No pericardial effusion.
findings: Pericardial effusion, __ mm, [circumferential / localised].
Right ventricular diastolic collapse with a plethoric inferior vena cava: tamponade physiology.

steps.label: Chest wall and ribs
steps.detail: Examine the point of maximal tenderness for cortical discontinuity and haematoma.
steps.look: High-frequency probe along the rib at the point of tenderness.
steps.normal: No rib fracture or chest-wall abnormality at the site of tenderness.
findings: Cortical step in the [ ] rib with an adjacent haematoma, compatible with a fracture.

steps.label: Uterus
steps.detail: Review uterine position, myometrium and cavity.
steps.look: Transabdominal survey, then transvaginal sagittal and transverse planes.
steps.normal: Uterus normal in size and appearance; endometrium [ ] mm.
findings: Degenerating fibroid __ mm with [heterogeneous / cystic] change at the site of pain.
Fluid or blood in the endometrial cavity.

steps.label: Pregnancy context
steps.detail: Describe pregnancy-related findings when relevant to the indication.
steps.look: Endometrial cavity for a gestational sac; adnexa for an extraovarian mass.
steps.normal: No intrauterine or ectopic pregnancy identified [pregnancy test negative].
findings: Intrauterine gestational sac with yolk sac [and embryo].
Positive pregnancy test with an empty uterus and an adnexal mass separate from the ovary, compatible with ectopic pregnancy.
Pregnancy of unknown location: no intrauterine or ectopic pregnancy seen.
steps.tip: An ectopic pregnancy moves separately from the ovary; a corpus luteum lies within it.

steps.label: Ovaries
steps.detail: Identify both ovaries and compare size, morphology and perfusion.
steps.look: Transvaginal scanning of each ovary with Doppler.
steps.normal: Both ovaries normal in size and appearance.
findings: Haemorrhagic cyst of the [right] ovary, __ mm, with a lace-like internal pattern and no internal flow.
Enlarged [right] ovary __ mm with peripheral follicles and oedematous stroma, suspicious for torsion.
Ruptured corpus luteum with surrounding echogenic fluid.
steps.tip: Preserved Doppler flow does not exclude torsion; an enlarged ovary with peripheral follicles is the key finding.

steps.label: Adnexa and tubes
steps.detail: Assess masses, tubal changes and torsion-related findings such as a twisted pedicle.
steps.look: Adnexal region between the uterus and pelvic sidewall; the pedicle for a whirlpool sign.
steps.normal: No adnexal mass or tubal abnormality.
findings: Thick-walled, fluid-filled tube (hydrosalpinx / pyosalpinx).
Complex adnexal collection, compatible with tubo-ovarian abscess in the appropriate clinical setting.
Whirlpool sign of the vascular pedicle.

steps.label: Free fluid and other causes
steps.detail: Assess the amount and echogenicity of pelvic fluid and visible non-gynaecological causes.
steps.look: Pouch of Douglas, then Morison pouch if haemoperitoneum is suspected; appendix and ureters.
steps.normal: Small physiological amount of free fluid only.
findings: Moderate echogenic free fluid extending to Morison pouch, compatible with haemoperitoneum.
Alternative cause: [appendicitis / ureteric stone / ovarian vein thrombosis].
steps.tip: Echogenic fluid in the upper abdomen in a pregnant patient suggests significant haemorrhage.

steps.label: Ovaries
steps.detail: Assess endometriomas, haemorrhagic content and ovarian position (kissing ovaries).
steps.look: T1 fat-suppressed and T2 images of both ovaries.
steps.normal: Both ovaries normal; no endometrioma.
findings: Endometrioma of the [right] ovary, __ mm: T1 hyperintense with T2 shading.
Kissing ovaries behind the uterus, indicating adhesions.
steps.tip: T2 shading of a T1-bright cyst is characteristic of an endometrioma.

steps.label: Anterior compartment
steps.detail: Inspect the bladder, vesicouterine pouch and distal ureters.
steps.look: Sagittal and axial T2 through the bladder dome and base.
steps.normal: Bladder wall and vesicouterine pouch normal; distal ureters normal.
findings: Bladder wall nodule __ mm at the [dome / base] with T2 low signal and bright foci.
Obliterated vesicouterine pouch with fibrosis.
Ureteric involvement with hydroureteronephrosis.

steps.label: Posterior compartment
steps.detail: Map uterosacral ligaments, torus uterinus, rectovaginal septum and pouch of Douglas.
steps.look: Sagittal and axial T2 along the uterosacral ligaments and behind the cervix.
steps.normal: Uterosacral ligaments, torus and rectovaginal space normal; pouch of Douglas patent.
findings: Thickened, nodular uterosacral ligaments [right / left / both].
Retrocervical (torus) nodule __ mm with fibrotic T2 low signal.
Obliteration of the pouch of Douglas.

steps.label: Bowel
steps.detail: Define the involved segment, depth of wall involvement and stenosis.
steps.look: Sagittal T2 along the rectosigmoid; distance from the anal verge.
steps.normal: No bowel involvement.
findings: Rectosigmoid nodule __ mm long, __ cm from the anal verge, involving the muscularis propria (mushroom-cap appearance).
Luminal narrowing of __%.

steps.label: Uterus and complications
steps.detail: Assess adenomyosis, hydronephrosis and other implants or adhesions.
steps.look: Sagittal T2 of the junctional zone; kidneys for hydronephrosis; abdominal wall scars.
steps.normal: No adenomyosis; no hydronephrosis.
findings: Adenomyosis with junctional zone thickening __ mm and T2-bright foci.
Hydroureteronephrosis from ureteric involvement.
Abdominal wall endometriosis in the caesarean section scar.
steps.tip: A normal MRI does not exclude superficial peritoneal endometriosis.

steps.label: Primary tumour
steps.detail: Identify the cervical epicentre and measure the tumour in three axes.
steps.look: High-resolution T2 perpendicular (oblique axial) and parallel to the cervical canal; DWI.
findings: Cervical tumour __ × __ × __ mm centred on the [anterior / posterior] lip.
Distance from the tumour to the internal os __ mm.
steps.tip: FIGO stage IB depends on size (2 cm and 4 cm thresholds); measure in three planes.

steps.label: Stroma and parametria
steps.detail: Assess the low-signal stromal ring and true extension into the parametrium on each side.
steps.look: Oblique axial T2 perpendicular to the cervix.
steps.normal: Preserved low-signal stromal ring; no parametrial invasion.
findings: Full-thickness stromal invasion with an intact outer stromal ring.
Disruption of the stromal ring with nodular tumour in the [left] parametrium (FIGO IIB).
steps.tip: Parametrial invasion needs tumour beyond the disrupted stromal ring; expansion or oedema alone is not enough.

steps.label: Vagina and pelvic sidewall
steps.detail: Describe vaginal extent, pelvic sidewall involvement and hydronephrosis.
steps.look: Sagittal T2 for vaginal extent; axial for sidewall and ureters.
steps.normal: No vaginal, sidewall or ureteric involvement.
findings: Extension to the upper two-thirds of the vagina (FIGO IIA).
Extension to the lower third of the vagina (FIGO IIIA).
Pelvic sidewall involvement or hydronephrosis (FIGO IIIB).

steps.label: Bladder and rectum
steps.detail: Differentiate contact from mucosal invasion of the bladder or rectum.
steps.look: Sagittal T2 of the bladder and rectal walls next to the tumour.
steps.normal: Fat planes with the bladder and rectum preserved.
findings: Tumour abuts the bladder wall with preserved low-signal muscle.
Tumour invades the bladder mucosa (FIGO IVA).
steps.tip: Bullous oedema of the bladder mucosa without tumour signal is not stage IVA.

steps.label: Nodes and other spread
steps.detail: Map suspicious pelvic and para-aortic nodes and other disease in the field.
steps.look: Axial T2 and DWI from the renal veins to the inguinal regions.
steps.normal: No suspicious pelvic or para-aortic nodes.
findings: Suspicious [right external iliac] node, short axis __ mm, round with heterogeneous signal (FIGO IIIC1r).
Suspicious para-aortic node (FIGO IIIC2r).
steps.tip: Nodal involvement upstages to IIIC regardless of the local extent; label it r (radiological).

steps.label: Uterus and tumour
steps.detail: Describe uterine anatomy, tumour location and size.
steps.look: Sagittal T2 and T2 perpendicular to the endometrial cavity; DWI.
findings: Endometrial tumour __ × __ × __ mm at the [fundus / body].
Uterus __ cm long with [fibroids / adenomyosis].

steps.label: Myometrial invasion
steps.detail: Assess the deepest invasion relative to the local myometrial thickness.
steps.look: T2 perpendicular to the tumour base, DWI and dynamic contrast images.
findings: Tumour confined to the endometrium with an intact junctional zone.
Myometrial invasion of less than 50% (__ of __ mm).
Myometrial invasion of 50% or more (__ of __ mm).
steps.tip: Adenomyosis, fibroids and a thinned myometrium make invasion assessment difficult; DWI and dynamic contrast help.

steps.label: Cervix
steps.detail: Distinguish endocervical glandular extension from cervical stromal invasion.
steps.look: Sagittal and oblique axial T2 of the cervix; delayed contrast phase.
steps.normal: No cervical involvement.
findings: Tumour extends into the endocervical canal with an intact cervical stroma.
Cervical stromal invasion.

steps.label: Extrauterine extent
steps.detail: Assess the serosa, adnexa, vagina, parametria, bladder and rectum.
steps.look: Axial and sagittal T2 around the uterus.
steps.normal: No extrauterine extension.
findings: Serosal breach with tumour in the [ ].
Adnexal involvement.
Invasion of the bladder or rectal mucosa.

steps.label: Nodes and distant sites
steps.detail: Describe pelvic and para-aortic nodes, peritoneal disease and other covered metastases.
steps.look: Axial T2 and DWI to the renal veins.
steps.normal: No suspicious nodes or peritoneal disease.
findings: Suspicious [left obturator] node, short axis __ mm.
Peritoneal deposits in the [ ].
steps.tip: FIGO 2023 staging includes pathology and molecular inputs that MRI cannot provide; report imaging extent.

steps.label: External fundal contour
steps.detail: Assess the external fundal shape independently of the cavity.
steps.look: True coronal plane along the long axis of the uterus (3D ultrasound or MRI).
steps.normal: Normal convex or flat external fundal contour.
findings: External fundal indentation of __ mm, more than 50% of the uterine wall thickness (bicorporeal uterus).
Straight external fundal contour.
steps.tip: The external fundal contour separates a septate from a bicorporeal uterus; measure it on a true coronal plane.

steps.label: Uterine cavities
steps.detail: Define the number, configuration and communication of the cavities.
steps.look: True coronal plane: internal indentation and septum length.
steps.normal: Single normal triangular cavity.
findings: Septate uterus: internal indentation __ mm, more than 50% of wall thickness, with a normal external contour (ESHRE/ESGE U2).
Hemi-uterus [with / without] a rudimentary horn (U4).
T-shaped (dysmorphic) cavity (U1).

steps.label: Cervix
steps.detail: Identify the number and configuration of cervical canals.
steps.look: Axial and coronal images through the cervix.
steps.normal: Single normal cervix.
findings: Double cervix (C2).
Septate cervix (C1).
Cervical aplasia (C4).

steps.label: Vagina
steps.detail: Assess longitudinal or transverse septa and obstructed compartments.
steps.look: Axial T2 through the vagina; sagittal for transverse septa.
steps.normal: Normal vagina.
findings: Longitudinal vaginal septum (V1/V2).
Obstructed hemivagina with haematocolpos.

steps.label: Associated anomalies
steps.detail: Look for renal anomalies, haematometra and a functional rudimentary horn.

steps.normal: No abscess; no supralevator extension.
findings: Abscess __ × __ × __ mm in the [ischioanal / intersphincteric] space.
Supralevator extension.
steps.tip: Supralevator extension changes the surgical approach; always look above the levator plane.

steps.label: Sphincters and context
steps.detail: Assess sphincter defects, setons, surgical changes and proctitis.
steps.look: Sphincter integrity on axial T2; rectal wall.
steps.normal: Sphincters intact; no seton; no proctitis.
findings: Seton in situ along the [ ] tract.
Sphincter defect at __ o'clock.
Proctitis, compatible with Crohn disease in the appropriate context.

steps.label: Rest and squeeze
steps.detail: Assess rectal configuration, the anorectal angle and anorectal junction position at rest and during squeeze.
steps.look: Lateral fluoroscopy in the seated position with contrast in the rectum (and small bowel and vagina when opacified).
steps.normal: Normal rectal configuration; anorectal angle narrows and the junction elevates on squeeze.
findings: Anorectal angle does not change on squeeze.
Low resting position of the anorectal junction.

steps.label: Strain and descent
steps.detail: Describe pelvic-floor descent and anorectal opening during strain.
steps.look: Maximal strain: anorectal junction relative to a stated bony landmark; anorectal angle opening.
steps.normal: Normal descent and opening of the anorectal angle on strain.
findings: Excessive pelvic floor descent of __ cm relative to [landmark].
Failure of the anorectal angle to open with a persistent puborectalis impression.
steps.tip: Measurements depend on the landmark; state it and do not import MRI H/M-line grading.

steps.label: Rectocele
steps.detail: Assess the anterior outpouching, its depth and emptying.
steps.look: Lateral view at maximal evacuation; depth beyond the expected anterior rectal wall.
steps.normal: No significant rectocele.
findings: Anterior rectocele __ cm deep with [complete emptying / contrast retention] after evacuation.

steps.label: Intussusception and enterocele
steps.detail: Identify intrarectal, intra-anal or external prolapse and small-bowel descent.
steps.look: Late evacuation images; small-bowel opacification between the rectum and vagina.
steps.normal: No intussusception, prolapse or enterocele.
findings: [Intrarectal / intra-anal] intussusception.
External rectal prolapse.
Enterocele descending into the rectovaginal space.
steps.tip: Poor effort underestimates prolapse; record the patient effort.

steps.label: Evacuation
steps.detail: Describe emptying, residual contrast and coordination.
steps.look: Evacuation phase and post-evacuation image.
steps.normal: Complete, coordinated evacuation.
findings: Partial evacuation with __ retained contrast.
Failed evacuation with paradoxical puborectalis contraction (spastic pelvic floor pattern).

steps.label: Orientation
steps.detail: Identify the uterus and ovaries as landmarks and the site of symptoms.
steps.look: Transvaginal survey; use probe pressure to find the point of maximal tenderness.
steps.normal: Uterus and ovaries identified and normal.
findings: Tenderness at the [right / left] pelvic side wall; uterus and ovaries normal.

steps.label: Bowel
steps.detail: Assess the pelvic bowel wall and adjacent inflammation.
steps.look: Sigmoid and rectum posterior to the uterus; compress to assess wall and fat.
steps.normal: Pelvic bowel normal.
findings: Sigmoid diverticulitis with an inflamed diverticulum and echogenic fat.
Rectal wall thickening __ mm with a hypoechoic mass (possible carcinoma).
Endometriotic nodule of the rectal wall.

steps.label: Appendix and focal inflammation
steps.detail: Describe a pelvic appendix or inflammatory focus only if demonstrated.
steps.look: Right side of the pelvis for a deep pelvic appendix.
steps.normal: Appendix not seen; no focal inflammatory abnormality.
findings: Inflamed pelvic appendix __ mm with surrounding inflamed fat.
Appendix seen and normal.

steps.label: Bladder and distal ureters
steps.detail: Inspect the visible bladder wall and distal ureters.
steps.look: Bladder base and trigone; distal ureters lateral to the cervix.
steps.normal: Bladder and distal ureters normal.
findings: Stone __ mm in the distal [right] ureter with ureteric dilatation.
Bladder wall mass __ mm.
steps.tip: Distal ureteric stones are often easier to see transvaginally than transabdominally.

steps.label: Fluid and limitations
steps.detail: Assess collections and the extent of the examination.
steps.look: Pouch of Douglas and paracolic regions; state which structures were not seen.
steps.normal: No pelvic collection; structures beyond the pelvis not assessed.
findings: Pelvic abscess __ mm.
Ascites with peritoneal nodules.
steps.tip: A negative transvaginal study does not exclude disease higher in the abdomen.

steps.label: Symptomatic region
steps.detail: Identify a focal abnormality at the site of maximal tenderness.
steps.look: Ask the patient to point to the pain and start there with graded compression.
steps.normal: No abnormality at the site of pain.
findings: Focal abnormality at the site of pain: [ ].
steps.tip: Graded compression displaces bowel gas and shows non-compressible inflamed structures.

steps.label: Bowel and appendix
steps.detail: Assess the appendix, bowel wall, peristalsis and inflamed fat.
steps.look: Graded compression in the right iliac fossa, left iliac fossa and along the colon.
steps.normal: Appendix normal (or not seen); no bowel wall thickening or inflamed fat.
findings: Acute appendicitis: non-compressible appendix __ mm with inflamed fat.
Sigmoid diverticulitis: inflamed diverticulum with echogenic fat.
Terminal ileal thickening with enlarged nodes (ileocaecitis).

steps.label: Liver, biliary tract and pancreas
steps.detail: Review the visible liver, gallbladder, bile ducts and pancreas.
steps.look: Subcostal and intercostal windows.
steps.normal: Liver, gallbladder, bile ducts and visible pancreas normal.
findings: Acute cholecystitis.
Dilated common bile duct __ mm.
Echogenic free gas anterior to the liver (perforated viscus).
steps.tip: Free gas appears as echogenic lines with reverberation anterior to the liver.

steps.label: Kidneys, bladder and aorta
steps.detail: Assess urinary obstruction and the visible aorta.
steps.look: Both kidneys for hydronephrosis; bladder; aorta for aneurysm.
steps.normal: No hydronephrosis; bladder normal; visible aorta not aneurysmal.
findings: [Right] hydronephrosis.
Abdominal aortic aneurysm __ mm.

steps.label: Pelvis and peritoneum
steps.detail: Review pelvic structures, free fluid and collections, and state the examination limits.
steps.look: Pouch of Douglas through a full bladder; Morison pouch.
steps.normal: No free fluid or collection; pelvic structures unremarkable.
findings: Free fluid in the pouch of Douglas and Morison pouch.
Collection __ mm in the [ ].
Examination limited by [gas / habitus].

steps.label: Coverage and landmarks
steps.detail: Follow bowel continuity and record which segments were examined.
steps.look: Survey with a curvilinear probe, then a high-frequency probe with graded compression; use the caecum, ascending and descending colon and sigmoid as landmarks.
steps.normal: Stomach, small bowel, terminal ileum and colon examined.
findings: [Segments] examined; [segments] not visualised because of [gas / habitus].
steps.tip: A segment that was not seen cannot be declared normal.

steps.label: Wall
steps.detail: Assess thickness, layering and symmetry under suitable distension.
steps.look: Measure a single wall perpendicular to the lumen; the five-layer gut signature.
steps.normal: Normal wall thickness with preserved layering.
findings: Wall thickening of the [ ] __ mm with preserved layering.
Wall thickening with loss of layering over __ cm.
steps.tip: Wall thickness depends on distension and probe pressure.

steps.label: Lumen and motility
steps.detail: Record diameter, contents, peristalsis and compressibility.
steps.look: Real-time observation of the segment.
steps.normal: Normal calibre, peristalsis and compressibility.
findings: Dilated fluid-filled loops __ mm with [increased / absent] peristalsis.
Non-compressible segment.
Intussusception (target appearance) in the [ ].

steps.label: Doppler
steps.detail: Optimise Doppler settings before assessing mural hyperaemia.
steps.look: Low-flow settings with a small colour box on the wall.
steps.normal: Normal mural flow.
findings: Increased mural flow.
Absent mural flow, raising concern for ischaemia.

steps.label: Surrounding tissues
steps.detail: Inspect mesenteric fat, nodes, fluid and complications.
steps.look: Mesentery around abnormal loops; free fluid; collections or tracts.
steps.normal: No inflamed fat, enlarged nodes, fluid or collection.
findings: Inflamed (echogenic) fat around the [ ].
Enlarged mesenteric nodes.
Collection or fistulous tract at [ ].
